subject: physics
question_text: Calculate the total translational kinetic energy of 1 g of helium gas (molar mass 4 g/mol) at 127 °C. (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Short Answer Question 8 (printed p.141). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The four-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: 1 g of helium of molar mass 4 is n = 0.25 mol; T = 127 °C = 400 K; E = (3/2)nRT = 1.5 × 0.25 × 8.31 × 400 = 1246.5 J, matching the brief's independently checked arithmetic.

steps.label: Given data and moles
lines: so number of moles n = 1/4 = 0.25 mol.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Convert both the mass to moles and the temperature to kelvin.
steps.why: The kinetic-energy formula needs the number of moles and the absolute temperature, neither of which is given directly, so both must be worked out first.
common_mistakes: Using 127 K directly instead of converting to the absolute scale, 400 K.
Forgetting to divide the mass by the molar mass to get moles.
steps.memory_tip: Divide by molar mass for moles; add 273 for kelvin.

steps.label: Formula
lines: n moles of an ideal gas:
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the formula in terms of n, R and T.
steps.why: Each molecule carries an average translational energy of (3/2)k_BT, and n moles hold N_A·n such molecules, which turns k_B into R.
common_mistakes: Using (3/2)RT for one mole and forgetting to multiply by n for a different amount of gas.
steps.memory_tip: Three-halves nRT — the same three-halves as the average energy per molecule.

steps.label: Substitution
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Substitute all four numbers before multiplying out.
steps.why: Each of the four numbers has already been justified in the earlier steps, so this line is a direct substitution with no new physics.
common_mistakes: Substituting 127 for T instead of the converted 400 K.
Multiplying only two of the four factors and stopping early.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply the four numbers in one line: 1.5, 0.25, 8.31, 400.

steps.label: Final kinetic energy
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. State the final value with its unit, joule.
steps.why: Multiplying the four factors together in order gives the total translational kinetic energy of the whole 1 g sample, not of one molecule.
common_mistakes: Reporting the energy of one molecule instead of the whole 0.25 mol sample.
Dropping the decimal and writing 12465 J or 124.65 J.
steps.memory_tip: Twelve hundred and forty-six point five joules — about 1.25 kJ.

insider_note: The two conversions, mass to moles and °C to kelvin, carry the first mark between them — a student who substitutes 127 for T or 1 for n loses the final answer even with the right formula.
